## Learning sequence

Complete Module 3 first. We distinguish individual outcomes from sample statistics, develop standard errors, then use them to construct intervals and plan precision.

| [2. Sampling Distributions and Standard Errors](02-sampling-distributions.qmd) | [2. Practice](exercises/02-sampling-distributions.qmd) |
| [3. Confidence Intervals for Means](03-confidence-intervals-for-means.qmd) | [3. Practice](exercises/03-confidence-intervals-for-means.qmd) |
| [4. Proportions and Sample-size Planning](04-proportions-and-sample-size.qmd) | [4. Practice](exercises/04-proportions-and-sample-size.qmd) |

Finish the [integrated review](05-sampling-and-estimation-review.qmd). Instructor answers are kept separately.

## Cases, readings, and evidence

The main textbook is Anderson et al. (2020), 8th edition. Selected Chapter 7 material develops sampling and sampling distributions; selected Chapter 8 material develops mean and proportion intervals and planning.

- EAI employees: population summaries p.308; sample summaries p.316; finite correction and CLT pp.323–324.
- Lloyd's spending: known-SD inputs p.357.
- Household credit-card balances: rounded sample summaries and t interval pp.367–368.
- Women golfers: survey counts and normal interval p.378; planning pp.380–381.

We use stated book parameters and summaries rather than introducing unverified observation files. Artificial simulations and original planning extensions are labeled. No new workbook-to-CSV match is claimed.
